title: Let me think
description: Give me a moment to consider my answer.
details:
Example: Let me think. Thursday might work.

Usage: A natural way to pause while keeping your turn to speak.

title: How do I put this?
description: I’m choosing how to explain something carefully.
details:
Example: How do I put this? It’s not quite what I expected.

Usage: Useful before a difficult or delicate explanation.

title: You know what?
description: I’ve just had a thought or made a decision.
details:
Example: You know what? Let’s get a taxi.

Usage: Informal; draws attention to what you’re about to say.

title: Actually…
description: I want to correct something or add a different fact.
details:
Example: Actually, I’m free tomorrow.

Usage: Can sound blunt when correcting someone; use a friendly tone.

title: By the way
description: I want to mention something on another topic.
details:
Example: By the way, your parcel arrived.

Usage: Introduce a side point or a new topic.

title: Anyway…
description: Let’s move on or return to the main topic.
details:
Example: Anyway, what time shall we meet?

Usage: Can also help end a conversation; avoid sounding dismissive.

title: Speaking of…
description: That topic reminds me of something related.
details:
Example: Speaking of holidays, have you booked yours?

Usage: Follow with the topic that connects the two points.

title: Come to think of it
description: I’ve just remembered or realised something.
details:
Example: Come to think of it, I’ve seen that film.

Usage: Use when a thought occurs to you during the conversation.

title: Sorry, go ahead
description: Please speak first or continue.
details:
Example: Sorry, go ahead. What were you saying?

Usage: Useful when you both start speaking at once.

title: Sorry to interrupt
description: I need to speak before you finish.
details:
Example: Sorry to interrupt, but your taxi’s here.

Usage: A polite interruption; leave space for the person to resume.

title: Go on
description: Please continue what you were saying.
details:
Example: You were telling me about your trip. Go on.

Usage: Here it encourages a story; the meaning changes in other contexts.

title: What happened next?
description: Tell me the next part of the story.
details:
Example: You missed the bus? What happened next?

Usage: Shows interest and encourages the person to continue.

title: Really?
description: Is that true? I’m interested or surprised.
details:
Example: I used to live in Spain. Really? Whereabouts?

Usage: Tone matters: it can express interest, surprise, or doubt.

title: How come?
description: Why is that?
details:
Example: I’m leaving early. How come?

Usage: Informal; if adding a clause, use How come you’re leaving?, not How come are you leaving?

title: What do you mean?
description: Can you explain what you’re saying?
details:
Example: What do you mean by flexible hours?

Usage: A neutral question with a gentle tone; a sharp tone can sound confrontational.

title: Could you say that again?
description: Please repeat what you said.
details:
Example: Sorry, could you say that again? I didn’t hear you.

Usage: A polite request when you missed something.

title: I didn’t catch that
description: I didn’t hear or understand that part.
details:
Example: Sorry, I didn’t catch your name.

Usage: Often followed by a request to repeat the words.

title: Do you mean…?
description: Is this what you’re trying to say?
details:
Example: Do you mean this Friday or next Friday?

Usage: Check a specific interpretation rather than guessing.

title: You know what I mean?
description: Do you understand the idea or feeling I’m describing?
details:
Example: It’s hard to switch off after work, you know what I mean?

Usage: Informal; seeks understanding rather than testing the listener.

title: Where were we?
description: What were we talking about before the interruption?
details:
Example: Sorry about the phone call. Where were we?

Usage: Use to return to a conversation after a distraction.
